critiques.description: thr-005 asserts that invoice submitters are unauthenticated, but its evidence list omits the only passage that documents this, so the claim is not currently tied to its supporting evidence.
critiques.rationale: The threat description and preconditions state that "Invoice submitters are unauthenticated external users" and rely on this to motivate ease of abuse. The cited evidence evd-001, evd-002, and evd-006 describe the LLM-based agent, the invoice-submission workflow, and tracing, but do not say anything about authentication. The fact that submitters "are not otherwise authenticated to the workflow" appears only in evd-005. Because thr-005 does not list evd-005 among its evidence_ids, its unauthenticated-submitter claim is effectively unsupported under the evidence policy, even though a suitable passage exists. The threat should either add evd-005 as supporting evidence or explicitly mark the unauthenticated property as an assumption/inference.

critiques.description: map-050’s applicability reasoning depends on invoice submitters being unauthenticated, but the mapping does not cite the evidence that establishes this property.
critiques.rationale: The applicability_reason for req-TPI-002 says it applies because "each invoice submission by an unauthenticated external user" triggers processing the system does not originate. The mapping cites evd-001, evd-002, and evd-006, which establish that users submit invoices, that the agent processes them via a hosted model provider with tracing, but they say nothing about authentication. The only passage that documents that "submitters are not otherwise authenticated to the workflow" is evd-005. Evidence assessment eas-071 correctly includes evd-005 when analysing this mapping, but map-050 itself does not. To align the mapping with the evidence policy, either evd-005 should be added to its evidence_ids or the "unauthenticated" aspect should be explicitly treated as an assumption/inference rather than a documented fact.
